The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election took place on 3 May 2012 to elect members of Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council in Greater Manchester, England. This election was part of the local elections held simultaneously across England, Scotland, and Wales.

In the case of Stockport, the election involved one third of the council's seats, as Stockport operates a system where one third of the councillors are elected each year for three years, with a break in the fourth year when elections to the Greater Manchester County Council would have been held. However, this county council was abolished in 1986.

During the 2012 election, the council seats were contested across various wards in the borough. Each ward elects one councillor for a four-year term. The usual range of local issues and national political trends influenced voter behavior.

The political composition of the council prior to the election included members from different parties, with the Liberal Democrats having been historically strong in Stockport, along with both Labour and Conservative councillors.

Following the 2012 election, there might have been shifts in the balance of power on the council. However, detailed results such as which party won specific wards, how many seats each party captured, or how this affected the overall control of the council might require referencing specific election data from the Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council or coverage from news archives from that time. 

Such elections often impact local policies on planning and development, education, transportation, environmental management, and community services, making them significant in shaping the local governance and day-to-day administration of the borough.
